It is an Engishiki-listed shrine near the summit of {{ill|Mount Tochihara|Q11535103|qid=Q11535103}}.

=== Chronology ===
* Founded on {{ill|November 11|Q2987|qid=Q2987}}, Tenpy? 2 ({{ill|730|Q23563|qid=Q23563}})
* In April, Ten'an 2 ({{ill|858|Q30371|qid=Q30371}}), received Junior Fourth Rank, Lower ("{{ill|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|Q1052905|qid=Q1052905}}")
* On {{ill|June 23|Q2668|qid=Q2668}}, J?gan 6 ({{ill|864|Q25041|qid=Q25041}}), received Senior Fourth Rank, Lower ("{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}")
* On {{ill|November 4|Q2994|qid=Q2994}}, J?gan 8 ({{ill|866|Q23872|qid=Q23872}}), received Junior Third Rank ("Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku")
* Burned down in a fire during the {{ill|Bunki|Q1324885|qid=Q1324885}} era (1501-1504)

=== Miyaza ritual ===
The Miyaza ritual of Hahime Shrine is designated as an intangible cultural property by Shimoichi Town. Two parishioners are selected as yearly ritual households (older seat and younger seat), each only once in a lifetime, and they serve the shrine for one year. On the festival day only, the main hall is opened, a "transfer of divine spirit" is performed to ritual streamers, which are worshipped for seven days. At the end of September, both ritual households host relatives and associates and hold ceremonial offerings<ref>[http://www.town.shimoichi.lg.jp/0000000016.html Hahime Shrine] - Shimoichi Town, accessed July 13, 2017.</ref>.
